original_question: If X1 and X2 are Gushel-Mukai varieties of the same dimension and their Kuznetsov components are equivalent, must X1 and X2 be birational?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 7.18 in Section 7.3: the Birational Categorical Torelli conjecture for Gushel-Mukai varieties (restated from [90, Conjecture 1.7]).
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact logical content of the paper's target statement: it asks about two Gushel-Mukai varieties X1 and X2, assumes they have the same dimension, assumes an equivalence of Kuznetsov components, and asks whether this forces X1 and X2 to be birational. It also correctly targets the birational Gushel-Mukai problem, not the neighboring stronger question about isomorphism of Gushel-Mukai fourfolds under compatibility with degree-shift functors.
missing_details: For a fully stand-alone formulation, specify the ambient base field convention used in the paper: varieties are taken over an algebraically closed field K.
Say explicitly that X1 and X2 are smooth projective Gushel-Mukai varieties.
Define the notation Ku(X_i) as the Kuznetsov component of Db(X_i).
Replace the informal phrase 'their Kuznetsov components are equivalent' by the precise categorical statement that there exists an exact K-linear equivalence Ku(X1) ≅ Ku(X2).

To stay paper-faithful, make clear that no extra hypothesis such as compatibility with degree-shift functors or Fourier-Mukai type is part of Conjecture 7.18; those belong to nearby but different questions.
refined_question: Let X1 and X2 be smooth projective Gushel-Mukai varieties over an algebraically closed field K, of the same dimension, and let Ku(X_i) denote the Kuznetsov component of Db(X_i). If there exists an exact K-linear equivalence Ku(X1) ≅ Ku(X2), must X1 and X2 be birational?
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Conjecture 7.18, which is the paper's explicit Gushel-Mukai birational reconstruction conjecture. The nearby Question 7.16 is different: it asks for isomorphism of Gushel-Mukai fourfolds under an equivalence commuting with degree-shift functors, and Remark 7.17 records a related Hodge-theoretic consequence. The introduction and Section 6.5 explain why the Gushel-Mukai problem is formulated birationally rather than isomorphically: the paper notes the existence of non-isomorphic but birational Gushel-Mukai threefolds with equivalent Kuznetsov components. So the right refinement is not to broaden or change the statement, but only to add the standing field/category conventions and the notation Ku(X).
